thread:
maria_support: Customer report — structured (JSON) streaming response truncated mid-object. Happens on hosted API (us-east). They get partial JSON (last bytes end inside an object) so client parser throws.

kevin_support: Thanks — can you paste the request id / trace id and the minimal curl you used? also which SDK/version and whether it's http2 or http1.1? :thinking:

maria_support: Repro snippet from customer (redacted keys):
```
curl -N -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses \ 
  -d '{"model":"gptx-2","stream":true,"response_format":{"type":"json"},"input":"generate json objects"}'
```
They say the response starts streaming and then abruptly stops — client sees something like:
```
{"id":"r1","choices":[{"text":"{\"user\":\"john\",\"items\": [\"a\"","...EOF"}]}
```
so the trailing braces/array close are missing. Happened ~6 times today, different customers, intermittent. Rooted to production route: /v1/responses.

sam_runtime: Two quick suspects: edge/proxy idle/timeout or an upstream worker hitting a hard stop during background token refresh. Also worth checking whether SSE/chunk boundaries align with JSON tokens. If a chunk cut happens inside a structural token you'll get invalid JSON.

raj_edge: We had an edge deploy yesterday 2026-03-14 03:12 UTC (build 2026.03.14-7b9f). No alerts but there was a spike in half-closed sockets around that time. Could be NGINX proxy_read_timeout or Cloudflare handing off RST on certain keepalive windows.

kevin_support: Customer gave a trace-id: trace_8b7c9a2f. Also they are using our JS SDK v1.4.2 over http2 by default. They said switching to non-streaming (one-shot) works fine.

sam_runtime: Please try two quick repro variants and paste results back:
1) Force http1.1: add `--http1.1` to curl.
2) Use curl with no buffering and verbose to watch connection close: `curl -N -v --http2 https://...` (or remove http2).
Also collect the response headers (esp `Content-Length`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `Connection`, and any `x-request-id`/`x-redwood-trace`).

maria_support: I asked customer to run both. They ran http1.1 and it still truncated. With `-v` they saw the remote close after some bytes and then `recv` returned 0.

sam_runtime: That points more at an upstream process or intermediate reset rather than pure http2 semantics. Next: can we grab edge logs for trace_8b7c9a2f and the corresponding backend request id? raj_edge, can you pull?

raj_edge: Pulling logs now. Also checking firewall and LB health for that timeframe. If the edge saw `FIN`/`RST` from backend we should have packet boundary markers in the logs. Will also check our `proxy_buffering` thresholds.

deploy-bot: edge-deploy/2026.03.14-7b9f pushed at 03:12 UTC — impact window 03:10-03:20. No config changes to streaming headers, but we rotated a sidecar image (conn handling) in some nodes.

sam_runtime: Useful mitigation for customers in the short-term: 1) enable structured streaming with heartbeat frames or suffix newlines per object so parsers can tolerate boundary splits, 2) client-side retry logic that reconnects and attempts to stitch frames (if idempotent). We'll also add an internal test that intentionally injects chunk-boundary splits to validate parser robustness.

raj_edge: Got the edge log entry. For trace_8b7c9a2f we see the connection to upstream closed with `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header`. Upstream request id: u-54c3b. Escalating u-54c3b to runtime.

sam_runtime: Thanks — pulling runtime logs for u-54c3b. I see worker crash due to an unrelated mem spike at 03:13:02 which caused the response stream to be cut. Crashtrace: `OOM in vtable allocator` in a background plugin — looks like a rare path triggered by certain prompts.

maria_support: Can you confirm that an OOM would cause ambiguous EOF and produce a truncated stream? Customer-facing explanation needs to be clear.

sam_runtime: Yes — if the process is killed while streaming, TCP will close and client gets EOF mid-json. We'll label this a P1 for the crash. Repro plan: run the failing prompt through a stress harness against the same runtime image and monitor mem. Also add guardrails to ensure the stream ends with a closing chunk on SIGTERM where possible (best-effort).

raj_edge: For mitigation, we can enable a temporary routing policy to prefer stable nodes (no recent sidecar rotation) and increase upstream read timeouts for that pool to prevent premature resets while we patch.

kevin_support: I'll relay to customer: root cause likely upstream worker crash causing truncated stream; we're patching and will route them to stable nodes. ETA? :eyes:

sam_runtime: ETA for hotfix: revert faulty sidecar bump in edge pool in 2-3 hours, run mem-hardened runtime build tomorrow. I'll open a changelist and link it here when created.

maria_support: Thanks — I'll keep customer updated and collect any additional traces. Posting here the two debug commands I asked them to run (copy into incident ticket):
```
# verbose stream (shows connection close)
curl -N -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses

# force http1.1
curl -N -v --http1.1 -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses
```

deploy-bot: roll/edge-pool revert initiated for nodes with sidecar=2026.03.14-7b9f, targeting 6 nodes.

raj_edge: Revert in progress. Will monitor error rate and truncated-stream incidents.

kevin_support: Customer acknowledged. Marking this thread as escalated -> runtime, edge. I'll add the ticket link to the case. :thumbsup:

maria_support: Closing loop here for now — will re-open if we see more truncation after revert/patch. Thanks everyone.
